name: Alprazolam
summary: Diazepam's opposite, and instructive next to it. Alprazolam comes on fast and leaves in about eleven hours, which sounds safer than a drug that lingers for a week. In practice the short half-life is the problem: it falls far enough between doses for withdrawal to start before the next one, so the drug creates the anxiety it is prescribed for.
mechanism: The same GABA-A mechanism as diazepam, but with higher potency per milligram and faster onset. It also has some specific anti-panic activity not shared by all benzodiazepines. The rapid onset and short duration is the combination most associated with dependence across all drug classes.

sublingual.note: Slightly faster onset; total exposure is essentially the same.

pathways.name: Alpha-hydroxyalprazolam
pathways.note: Active but short-lived and present at low concentrations; contributes modestly.

risk: Compare this curve with diazepam's. Alprazolam's peak-to-trough swing on the same schedule is far wider, and it is that swing — not the average level — that drives interdose withdrawal, clock-watching and escalation.
Because it is cleared almost entirely by CYP3A4, inhibitors raise levels sharply. Grapefruit juice, ketoconazole, clarithromycin and some antiretrovirals can substantially increase exposure.
It is strongly associated with anterograde amnesia at ordinary doses, especially with alcohol — people act, and do not remember acting.

Withdrawal from short-acting benzodiazepines is faster in onset and more severe than from long-acting ones, and can include seizures. Stopping needs a slow taper, often after switching to a longer-acting benzodiazepine.
Counterfeit alprazolam tablets are common and have been found to contain fentanyl or novel benzodiazepines.
